- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥1.0) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast slightly, especially after sharp spikes.
- When sentiment is consistently negative (≤-1.0), model often underestimates; increase forecast modestly, particularly if recent price is trending down.
- Model frequently overshoots after strong upward sentiment spikes; apply a “cool-down” correction by reducing forecast by 1–3% in the next 3–5 periods.
- If sentiment flips from positive to negative mid-horizon, model often fails to adjust; apply a downward bias correction starting from the sentiment flip point.
- Mean reversion is strong in 30-day forecasts; if forecast is >10% above recent 10-day average, reduce by 1–2% per period until convergence.
- If sentiment history shows high volatility (alternating +/–), model tends to overfit short-term noise; smooth forecasts using 3-period moving average or dampen volatility-weighted components.
